## Left open by the earlier read (RD-150)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule L02 (Major). Problem: The statutory sentence stacks conspiracy, co-principals, accomplices and accessories. Conspiracy is explained afterward, but the three participation roles never receive simple meanings. A Grade 5 reader cannot understand that part of the teaching.
   > Section $11(c)$ covers private individuals "who participate in conspiracy as co-principals, accomplices or accessories" with public officials or employees in a violation of the Code.
2. Rule B08 (Minor). Problem: The numeral in Article 8 is outside inline math delimiters. It is a statute identifier, so this is the optional identifier-only formatting issue described by the brief. Monetary amounts and the other visible numeric references use inline math.
   > Under the Revised Penal Code (Article 8), a conspiracy exists when two or more persons agree to commit a crime and decide to commit it.

   Reader's note: Conspiracy and penal liabilities receive meanings, but co-principals, accomplices and accessories remain unexplained legal terms.
